subject: Hannah, mother of Samuel
note: Evidence for Hannah's Bible figure page. A thin record (1 Samuel 1:1-2:21 only), so a short page: six moments, no miracles section (the birth of Samuel is told among the moments as the Bible tells it: the LORD remembered her), no death section (the Bible says nothing of her end), one section of her own: her song beside Mary's, with the Catholic Encyclopedia's and the Lutheran calendar's words for the likeness. Every Bible line quotes the BSB (shared/bsb-berean-standard-bible.txt). Not Anna, the mother of Mary: the myth says so, from the Catholic Encyclopedia.

life.text: Hannah is named only in 1 Samuel 1 and 2 (1:2 to 2:21).
life.source: grep of shared/bsb-berean-standard-bible.txt for 'Hannah': 19 verses, all in 1 Samuel 1:2-2:21.

life.text: Elkanah of Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim; two wives, Hannah and Peninnah; Peninnah had children, Hannah none; yearly worship at Shiloh where Eli's sons were priests; the double portion 'for he loved her'; the rival's taunts; 'Am I not better to you than ten sons?'
After eating at Shiloh Hannah stood; Eli sat by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD; she prayed and wept and vowed a son to the LORD all his days, no razor on his head.

Eli watched her mouth; she prayed in her heart, lips moving, voice unheard; he thought her drunk ('How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!'); her answer (poured out her soul, not a wicked woman); 'Go in peace'; she ate and her face was no longer downcast.
Home to Ramah; the LORD remembered her; Samuel born and named 'Because I have asked for him from the LORD'; she stayed home until he was weaned; Elkanah: 'Do what you think is best'.

Weaned, the boy was brought to Shiloh with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour and a skin of wine; brought to Eli; 'I prayed for this boy'; dedicated to the LORD for life; her song (2:1-10); Elkanah home to Ramah, the boy ministering before Eli (2:11).
Samuel in a linen ephod; each year his mother made him a little robe; Eli's blessing; three sons and two daughters; the boy grew up in the presence of the LORD. Her last mention.
Nazirite: 'no razor shall touch his head' is the Nazirite vow's mark (Numbers 6:2, 5); Samson's mother told the same (Judges 13:5).
Samuel: confirmed as a prophet (3:20), judged Israel all his life (7:15), anointed Saul from a flask of oil (10:1) and David from the horn of oil (16:13). Eli very old (2:22).
Mary's song, Luke 1:46-55: lines paired on the page with 1 Samuel 2:1, 4, 5, 8 (Luke 1:47, 52, 53, 48).
life.source: Luke 1:46-55 (BSB). The likeness in the sources' words: Catholic Encyclopedia (1910), 'Magnificat': 'The Magnificat is in many places very similar in thought and phrase to the Canticle of Anna (1 Samuel 2:1-10)' (people/hannah/cathen-magnificat.txt); LCMS, Commemorations, 2 September: 'This song foreshadows the Magnificat, the Song of Mary centuries later (Lk 1:46-55).' (shared/lsb-calendar.txt; not quoted on the page, the LCMS text is not public domain).

life.text: Her name: Hebrew for grace; Anna in Greek and Latin; Anne in English.
life.source: Catholic Encyclopedia (1907), 'St. Anne': 'Anne (Hebrew, Hannah, grace; also spelled Ann, Anne, Anna)'; LCMS 2 September: 'The name Hannah derives from the Hebrew word for grace'; Augustine, City of God 17.4: 'whose very name, which is Hannah, means His grace'. Gregory Nazianzen (NPNF2-07, from the Greek) writes 'Anna'.

life.text: In art: Jan Victors (1643, Dordrecht; 1645, Berlin), Gerbrand van den Eeckhout (Ashmolean, 1660-63, and another c. 1665), Arent de Gelder (c. 1710), Samuel van Hoogstraten (drawing), the Rembrandt studio (Edinburgh): Eeckhout, de Gelder and van Hoogstraten were Rembrandt's pupils.
life.source: Wikimedia Commons, Category:Hannah, mother of Samuel in paintings, and the files listed under pictures.

fathers.text: Cyprian: Hannah 'a type of the Church', prayed silently from the heart, with faith; 'She spoke with hidden prayer, but with manifest faith...'
fathers.source: Cyprian, On the Lord's Prayer (Treatise 4), chapter 5, tr. R. E. Wallis, ANF 5 (people/hannah/cyprian-lords-prayer.txt)

fathers.text: Chrysostom: tears for God alone, 'such as were Hannah's'; 'her tears alone uttered a cry more clear than any trumpet. And because of this, God also opened her womb, and made the hard rock a fruitful field.'
fathers.source: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 6, tr. Prevost, NPNF1-10 (shared/npnf110.txt)

fathers.text: Chrysostom: 'Imitate Hannah's example'; 'Who amongst you would not rather that his son should become a Samuel than that he should be king of the whole world ten thousand times over?'
fathers.source: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Ephesians, Homily 21 (on Ephesians 6:1-4), Oxford translation revised by Gross Alexander, NPNF1-13 (shared/npnf113.txt)

fathers.text: Gregory Nazianzen: 'Anna even before Samuel was born promised him to God, and after his birth consecrated him at once...' (urging mothers not to delay their infants' baptism).
fathers.source: Gregory of Nazianzus, Oration 40, On Holy Baptism, chapter 17, NPNF2-07 (shared/npnf207.txt)

fathers.text: Augustine: her song is prophecy of the Church; 'whose very name, which is Hannah, means His grace'; 'when as yet no one was king over that people, whence, if she did not prophesy, did she say ... He gives strength to our kings, and shall exalt the horn of His Christ?'; she bore three males and two females afterward.
fathers.source: Augustine, The City of God, book 17, chapter 4, tr. Marcus Dods, NPNF1-2 (people/hannah/augustine-city-of-god-17.txt)

jewish.text: Seven prophetesses: Sarah, Miriam, Deborah, Hannah, Abigail, Huldah and Esther. Hannah a prophetess for 'my horn is exalted': David and Solomon, anointed from a horn, kept their kingship; Saul and Jehu, anointed from a flask, did not.
jewish.source: Babylonian Talmud, Megillah 14a, William Davidson English (CC BY-NC; paraphrased, never quoted) (people/hannah/sefaria-Megillah.14a.txt)

jewish.text: Rules of prayer from Hannah (Rav Hamnuna): focus the heart; enunciate with the lips; do not raise the voice in the Amida; a drunk may not pray.
First day of Rosh Hashanah: Genesis 21 ('And the Lord visited Sarah'), haftarah the account of Hannah (1 Samuel 1:1-2:10); by tradition both women were remembered on Rosh Hashanah.

legend.text: St Anne, Mary's mother, is not in the Bible; her name and story come from the Protoevangelium of James (earliest form about AD 150); 'Since this story is apparently a reproduction of the biblical account of the conception of Samuel, whose mother was also called Hannah, even the name of the mother of Mary seems to be doubtful.'

feasts.text: Orthodox: Prophetess Hannah the mother of the Prophet Samuel, 9 December (OCA), with a troparion (tone 2) and kontakion (tone 4); the same day as the Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos by Saint Anna. The kontakion says she saw things far off as if near (paraphrased; OCA translation not quoted).
feasts.source: OCA, lives for 9 December (people/hannah/oca-dec9-list.txt, oca-hannah-life.txt, oca-hannah-troparia.txt)

feasts.text: Lutheran, Missouri Synod: Hannah, 2 September; remembered for keeping the vow she made before her son's birth.

Catholic: no day for Hannah. The Roman Martyrology keeps Samuel, prophet, on 20 August; no entry for his mother in any month of the 2004 edition (English at GCatholic, all 24 half-month pages searched for Samuel/Hannah/Anna) nor in the 1916 edition (whose Anna, 1 September, is the prophetess of Luke 2).
Anglican: not on the Church of England, Episcopal (LFF 2022) or ELCA calendars; the Church of England's Common Worship: Daily Prayer has canticle 21, A Song of Hannah (1 Samuel 2.1,2,3b-5,7,8).

could_not_verify: No Orthodox icon of Hannah with a large, clear face and a public-domain licence was found on Commons: the Moscow Eleusa medallions are CC BY-SA photos; the Paris Psalter miniature (fol. 428v) is under 500 px with a tiny face; the Byzantine initial and Malnazar's Armenian miniature have small faces. So both pictures are Dutch paintings.
The OCA's troparion and kontakion are OCA translations (not public domain): paraphrased, not quoted.
A date for Cyprian's On the Lord's Prayer: not in the fetched texts; left out.

checked: Numbers: 'ten sons' (1 Samuel 1:8) and three sons and two daughters (2:21).

Feasts: Hannah on 2 September in shared/lsb-calendar.txt (its text also gives 'grace' and 'foreshadows the Magnificat'); the OCA's troparion page for 9 December ('you saw things far off as if they were near', paraphrased on the page); the old calendar 13 days later; Samuel on 20 August in the 2004 Roman Martyrology (people/hannah/roman-martyrology-2004-aug-gcatholic.txt).

Attributions: Cyprian, On the Lord's Prayer, chapter 5, 'a type of the Church'; Chrysostom's Homily 6 on Matthew (tears 'for God alone, such as were Hannah's') and Homily 21 on Ephesians ('Imitate Hannah's example'); Gregory Nazianzen, Oration 40; Augustine, City of God 17.4; the Talmud tidbits against the Sefaria files (Berakhot 31a, Megillah 14a and 31a, paraphrased, never quoted); the Catholic Encyclopedia on the Protoevangelium.
Rules: capitals for God; never 'St Hannah'; plain sentences; no section marks; tiles natural; licences as given; verify-quotes exits 0; saints-test passes.
